answeredQuestions: Q1: How do the three surfaces differ in SKILL.md section order, frontmatter fields and smart-routing blocks, and which form matches the sk-doc create-skill canon for a hub child?

label: The three surface SKILL.md files share the same top-level fields and read/search tool grant; their descriptions and versions vary by surface, while metadata consistently marks author OpenCode, family sk-code, and packetKind surface.

The three surface documents share the opening order WHEN THE HUB BUNDLES THIS, REFERENCE MAP, SMART ROUTING and the machine keys DEFAULT_RESOURCE, INTENT_SIGNALS, RESOURCE_MAP; Obsidian adds later source-tree, rules, and integration sections.

The sk-doc create-skill core frontmatter contract fits the shared fields, but its available packet scaffold is explicitly a primary workflow packet and the parent canon does not prescribe a surface body order; use a common surface skeleton with optional domain-specific sections.

The SKILLED and Webflow routing comments describe a parent union using only their named pair and omit Obsidian, while Obsidian says sibling surface maps generally and the hub lists all three; this is comment-level inconsistency and does not prove a route-map defect.
